headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write files and use allowlisted network while Taipy is local-only, creating default-path prompt, data, and workflow conflicts without direct evidence of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and run shell/subprocesses, while Taipy exposes no I/O surfaces and is not runnable. A shared filesystem bridge is plausible if the operator connects them, and AutoGPT may treat file content as trusted. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Taipy output is copied into files that AutoGPT reads as instructions
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable AutoGPT file-reading on untrusted folders
Insert a human review step before AutoGPT consumes Taipy outputs
Rename Taipy outputs to non-executable, data-only formats
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes, and Taipy has no network egress while AutoGPT's egress is allowlisted. The only plausible leakage path is a shared workspace or copied files, which is an unusual configuration here. Because the profiles do not document a shared workspace, the blast radius appears small and indirect.
conditions: IF the operator places confidential files in a shared folder
IF AutoGPT is configured to read those files and send their contents to its backend
mitigations: Keep confidential data out of any shared folder
Run AutoGPT on synthetic or redacted inputs
Confirm Taipy never receives secrets via copied artifacts
Review AutoGPT prompts before execution
requires-engineering: isolate each agent in separate storage volumes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while Taipy is a data-engineering tool that may also manipulate files or workflows, but its write scope is not documented here. Overlap on the filesystem is plausible, yet the absence of explicit Taipy write permissions makes the conflict uncertain; per rubric, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory
IF Taipy is configured to modify files that AutoGPT also edits
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Serialize file writes with a manual handoff
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project tree
Check for file locks before launching AutoGPT
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that Taipy could plausibly consume in a data-engineering workflow, but Taipy's authority to act is not documented and it is not runnable in the profile. The interaction is inferred rather than observed, so the risk is below high; however, if Taipy treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can propagate across work products.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests AutoGPT-produced files without validation
IF downstream jobs use those files as authoritative inputs
mitigations: Require schema validation on AutoGPT outputs
Add a human approval step before Taipy consumes generated artifacts
Compare generated facts against source data
Log provenance for each transferred artifact
requires-engineering: implement automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. With no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or policy mismatch, a compliance pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes
IF a deployment policy introduces residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Review residency and retention settings
Keep regulated data out of this pair
requires-engineering: add compliance policy checks to orchestration
